title: Cell-based test of 4-phenylbutyrate in VAMP2 disorders

sentences.text: This is a hypothesis, not a finding: its weakest link is the contested VAMP2 destabilization connection, because the reported instability concerns the SNARE complex rather than protein degradation and rescue.
Test whether 4-phenylbutyrate improves variant VAMP2 protein levels and neuronal release, variant by variant.
Use a VAMP2-variant neuronal model, prioritizing the characterized C-terminal SNARE-motif variants.
Prefer the existing VAMP2 electrophysiology and Munc18-1 rescue assays; establish their combined use for this VAMP2 drug test rather than assume it is validated.
Measure variant and wild-type VAMP2 protein levels, SNARE-complex formation, and evoked and spontaneous release with and without 4-phenylbutyrate.
Include untreated comparisons, wild-type comparisons, and a variant that augments spontaneous release as a negative control.

sections.heading: What result would change the plan

sentences.text: Continue preclinical investigation only if variant protein increases and evoked release recovers without increased spontaneous release.
Stop pursuing this rescue hypothesis if only wild-type protein rises or spontaneous release increases.
The VAMP2 evidence concerns nine variants in model systems, not demonstrated treatment benefit in patients.
4-phenylbutyrate's mechanism remains unresolved, and high concentrations and potential toxicity limit chemical-chaperone approaches.
